title: The artifact's own .skillignore suppresses evidence it contains, hiding it from its own audit
mechanism: The artifact ships a .skillignore that lists 'evidence/*' (and '*.log'). The artifact manifest says it contains evidence/audit.log, so the artifact's own configuration suppresses a file that the artifact itself contains. I-19 fires: an artifact may not use its own declarative config to hide its own contents from verification.
rationale: I-19 (no_self_suppression_of_evidence) is the exact predicate: `suppression.suppressed_contained(artifact_files)` must be empty. The other hooks do not fit: nothing uses an undeclared capability (I-17), no sealed artifact diverges (I-18), and no critical operation is flagged (I-20). The case deliberately includes files that the config does NOT suppress (SKILL.md, scripts/run.sh, and .skillignore itself) so the witness is a precise subset rather than 'the config exists'. Note that the matching pattern reported is the first one that matches in pattern order, and the witness reports file names, not patterns.

metadata.cwe: CWE-693: protection mechanism failure (self-suppression of audit evidence)
metadata.neutralization_semantics: Restricting the patterns to a scratch path ('tmp/*') that the artifact does not contain: the config still exists but no longer suppresses anything it ships.
